questions.question_text:
Which labelled point shows $(4,2)$?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(6,6);\draw[->](0,0)--(6.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,6.5)node[above]{$y$};\foreach \x/\y/\l in {4/2/A,2/4/B,4/4/C,2/2/D}{\fill(\x,\y)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$\l$};}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The horizontal and vertical coordinates were reversed.
The first coordinate was used for both positions.
The second coordinate was used for both positions.

questions.solution_text: Move $4$ units right, then $2$ units up, so the point is $A$.

questions.question_text:
Which labelled point shows $(1,5)$?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(6,6);\draw[->](0,0)--(6.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,6.5)node[above]{$y$};\foreach \x/\y/\l in {5/1/J,1/5/K,1/1/L,5/5/M}{\fill(\x,\y)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$\l$};}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The ordered pair was plotted vertical-first instead of horizontal-first.
Only the first coordinate was used for both movements.
Only the second coordinate was used for both movements.

questions.solution_text: Move right $1$ and up $5$, which lands at $K$.

questions.question_text:
Which labelled point correctly plots $(0,3)$?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(5,5);\draw[->](0,0)--(5.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,5.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(0,3)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$P$};\fill(3,0)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$Q$};\fill(3,3)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$R$};\fill(0,0)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$S$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The zero and three were placed on the wrong axes.
The nonzero coordinate was used in both positions.
Both coordinates were treated as zero at the origin.

questions.solution_text: With $x=0$, the point stays on the $y$-axis and moves up to $3$, so it is $P$.

questions.question_text:
Which labelled point correctly plots $(6,0)$?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.7]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(7,7);\draw[->](0,0)--(7.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,7.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(6,0)circle(2.5pt)node[above]{$W$};\fill(0,6)circle(2.5pt)node[right]{$X$};\fill(6,1)circle(2.5pt)node[above]{$Y$};\fill(0,0)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$Z$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The ordered pair was reversed, placing the point on the y-axis.
The zero coordinate was incorrectly plotted as one unit up.
The nonzero horizontal coordinate was ignored.

questions.solution_text: Move $6$ right and $0$ up, so the point is $W$.

options.why: The horizontal coordinate $3.5$ was plotted at $3$, ignoring the extra half unit.
The horizontal coordinate $3.5$ was plotted at $4$ instead of halfway between $3$ and $4$.

questions.solution_text: Move $3.5$ units right, then $5$ units up, so the point is $A$.

options.why: The vertical coordinate $2.5$ was plotted at $2$, ignoring the extra half unit.
The vertical coordinate $2.5$ was plotted at $3$ instead of halfway between $2$ and $3$.

questions.solution_text: Move $5$ units right, then $2.5$ units up, so the point is $R$.
